close_reason: Done in 22c103f. Added jmap_client_is_send_sync_clone compile-time trait-bound assertion test pinning JmapClient: Send + Sync + Clone. Extended JmapClient struct rustdoc to document the contract for consumers. Future refactor introducing non-Sync field (Rc/RefCell/Cell) fails the test in CI.
description:
client.rs:155-160 — pub struct JmapClient

The Clone derive auto-generates Clone iff all fields are Clone:
  - url::Url: Clone ✓
  - Arc<dyn AuthProvider>: Clone ✓
  - reqwest::Client: Clone ✓ (Arc-backed)
  - ClientConfig: Clone ✓

The struct ends up Send + Sync because:
  - url::Url is Send + Sync
  - Arc<dyn AuthProvider> requires AuthProvider: Send + Sync (which the trait requires at auth.rs:112)
  - reqwest::Client is Send + Sync
  - ClientConfig is Send + Sync

So `JmapClient: Send + Sync + Clone`. But the public docs do not state this contract. A caller relying on it (passing JmapClient by &Arc, sharing across tokio tasks) is exposed if a future internal refactor adds an Rc<...> or RefCell<...> field that breaks Sync. The Arc<dyn AuthProvider> blanket-impl maintenance note (auth.rs:107) flags one direction; the inverse direction — keeping JmapClient itself Send + Sync — is not flagged anywhere.

Recommendation:
1. Add a compile-time assert in the test module:
   ```rust
   #[test] fn jmap_client_is_send_sync() {
       fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}
       assert_send_sync::<JmapClient>();
   }
   ```
2. Document on the struct: "JmapClient is Send + Sync + Clone. Share by clone; the underlying reqwest::Client and Arc<dyn AuthProvider> are reference-counted."

The same gap applies to WsSession. It contains SplitSink/SplitStream over a MaybeTlsStream<TcpStream>. The Send-ness of those depends on tungstenite's internal types. A compile-time assert would lock the contract.
title: JmapClient lacks Send/Sync trait bounds in docs; AuthProvider trait-object requires Send + Sync at compile time
